summary: Brook Ziporyn is a scholar in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago (~1980–1984) and the University of Michigan (PhD). He held posts at Northwestern University (attested 2004) and the University of Chicago (~2013).
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.
Bruce Cameron Hall is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as an assistant editor at William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD from Columbia University under Alex Wayman, also studying with Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln is a historian of religions who studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1970–1976) under Mircea Eliade. He taught at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1993).
Bruce M. Knauft studied at the University of Michigan. He held a post as the Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University (attested 2016).
Bruce M. Sullivan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held an academic post at Northern Arizona University.

Bruce Matthews is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed graduate studies at McMaster University. He served as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Peradeniya and held a professorship at Acadia University (~1976).

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and as an associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens was a scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO (1969), University of Louvain (1972–1977), KU Leuven (~1977–1986), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich studied at Munich, Göttingen (Dr. phil. ~1882–1885), and Breslau (Habilitation 1880–1892). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was a professor at the University of Breslau (~1892–1918, 1921–1928) and Heidelberg (~1918–1934).

Bruno Lindner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (1871–1873) and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He served as a Privatdocent at the University of Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold studied at Leipzig (~1894–1896) and Berlin (~1896–1898), focusing on Buddhist studies and Japanology. In Japan, he taught at the First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.
Bruno Schindler, a scholar of Sinology, studied under August Conrady (~1910–1919). He founded Asia Major in 1923 and worked as an editor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone, later serving as an assistant professor of religious studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David F. Germano. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he became the John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University (attested 2008–2021).

Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991). Around 1996, he was appointed professor in the Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese departments at Vassar College.
Bryce Ryan was an academic working in Indology and related fields. Over the course of his career, he held academic appointments at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.
